key_insight: Lift-element network modes link vortex-gust impingement to a thickened airfoil shear layer and identify perturbations that produce sustained lift increases or decreases.
engineering_relevance: These cause-and-effect pathways could guide actuator placement and timing to manage transient aerodynamic loads.
method: Construct a dynamic network weighted by local lift-element changes induced by vorticity perturbations.
Use network broadcast analysis to extract forcing–response mode pairs.
Compare lift-element modes with Biot–Savart network modes.
evidence_signal: Three-dimensional NACA 0012 flows with a Taylor vortex gust at Reynolds number 1000 show that Biot–Savart-mode perturbations amplify or attenuate gust-induced lift variation, while lift-element-mode perturbations yield sustained lift shifts.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish performance at higher Reynolds numbers or demonstrate a practical closed-loop actuator implementation.
paper_title: Lift-element-based dynamic network of vortex gust-airfoil interactions
